Messages.Author: David Hyatt
Messages.Body:
(1) Can Dreams of the Sphinx be tapped when it is not your turn
to increase your hand size by 2? We have ruled that it can be.

(2) If a vampire with no blood has Society of Leopold on him during
untap, is he burned? The card (Jyhad version) reads that the vampire
loses 1 blood or is burned, Methuselah's choice. If the vampire cannot
lose 1 blood because he has none to lose, does that mean he is automatically
burned? I would say, "Yes, that vampire is kindling."

(3) I thought of a cute combo today. The two cards involved are
Might of the Camarilla and Redeem the Lost Soul.

Might of the Camarilla forces everyone to burn a vampire
in their inactive region if the vote is successful. Assume
that the vampire burned has a capacity of 10 or 11.

Next turn, you play Redeem the Lost Soul for a blood gain
of 5!

Anyway, that was my Jyhad/Vampire rambling for the day...

======================================================================
Dave Hyatt
http://www.shadowland.org/vampire/

Messages.Author: Zaphod Beeblebrox
Messages.Body:
David Hyatt (d-h...@cs.uiuc.edu) wrote:
: (2) If a vampire with no blood has Society of Leopold on him during

: untap, is he burned? The card (Jyhad version) reads that the vampire
: loses 1 blood or is burned, Methuselah's choice. If the vampire cannot
: lose 1 blood because he has none to lose, does that mean he is automatically
: burned? I would say, "Yes, that vampire is kindling."

This is how we have always played, yes. One or the other,
losing one blood or being burned, must take place, and if one
is impossible, the other must happen. It's fairly useless,
otherwise, and not nearly as much fun. :) Other effects, such
as hunting grounds, may give a vampire blood before you must
choose, of course, to keep it from being burned.

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
David Hyatt (d-h...@cs.uiuc.edu) wrote:
: (1) Can Dreams of the Sphinx be tapped when it is not your turn

: to increase your hand size by 2? We have ruled that it can be.

Hmm. A knee jerk reation tells me, yes, that's legal... but then I
reread the card. The sentence in question is:

"Tap this card to draw two cards and increase your hand size by
two until the end of your turn"

This sentence seems to indicate that you can only do this DURING your turn,
so that you can put the cards back at the end of your turn. So no, I don't
think you can tap it whenever you want... only during your turn. If you
could tap it whenever you wanted, you could get an increase of four cards,
as in:

"Tap it just before my turn begins to get two cards. Untap as normal
at the beginning of my turn, and I keep the two cards 'cuz my turn hasn't
ended yet. Tap it again to get two more. Return all four at the end
of my turn."

Again, _I_ think (feel free to wait for a ruling) that the modifying text
"...until the end of your turn" indicates that it can only be done during
your turn.

: (2) If a vampire with no blood has Society of Leopold on him during

: untap, is he burned? The card (Jyhad version) reads that the vampire
: loses 1 blood or is burned, Methuselah's choice. If the vampire cannot
: lose 1 blood because he has none to lose, does that mean he is automatically
: burned? I would say, "Yes, that vampire is kindling."

Not sure here... typically, if you can't burn blood that you are supposed
to, you just ignore the effect. Not sure how it applies to the Society...

: (3) I thought of a cute combo today. The two cards involved are

: Might of the Camarilla and Redeem the Lost Soul.
:
: Might of the Camarilla forces everyone to burn a vampire
: in their inactive region if the vote is successful. Assume
: that the vampire burned has a capacity of 10 or 11.

I only have the spoiler list to go by, so here's a question: does Might
of the Cam. burn ACTIVE or INACTIVE vampires? The spoiler list indicates
active... but otherwise it seems reasonable. And if it is an "active"
vampire (and not just a random empty big inactive one) then you probably
won't be getting anything for free because of any pool that you invested
making it active in the first place.

-spongy
